taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs 1-2 m; FNA 5-25 dm, canes erect.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs to 25 dm.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves deciduous.

traits.stem_clump.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: canes sent up from spreading roots in patches and thickets.

traits.spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): armed or unarmed: prickles absent or sparse to dense.

traits.spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): prickles erect, weak, 1-4 mm, broad-based.

traits.bark_colour.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): branchlets brown or reddish brown; sRGB by eye.

traits.leaf_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaflets mid green above, white beneath.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves pinnately compound.

traits.division_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pinnately compound.

traits.division_order.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets unlobed or 2-lobed.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet stalked, the side ones sessile: odd-pinnate.

traits.leaflets.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 3-5 (to 7); Flora of China: 5-7, rarely 3.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 10 cm to 25 cm long with the petiole.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petiole 3-6 cm.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 3-8 cm long; FNA terminal leaflet 7-15 cm.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 1.5-4.5 cm wide; FNA terminal 4-11 cm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet ovate to lanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet apex acute to attenuate; Flora of China shortly acuminate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins serrate to doubly serrate.

traits.leaf_hairs_beneath.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets strongly white-tomentose beneath.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal and axillary, racemiform; Flora of China short racemes.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): (1-)3-7 (to 20) flowers.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: short racemes 3 cm to 8 cm long.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pedicel 1-2 cm.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers 1-1.5 cm across.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white to greenish white, 5-10 mm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white to greenish white; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): aggregate fruit 1-1.4 cm across; FNA 0.5-2 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits usually red; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits globose to conic; Flora of China subglobose.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus idaeus subsp. strigosus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering May to July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: fruit ripe July to September.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a patch of upright brownish canes with weak prickles, pinnate leaves white beneath, small white flowers in short clusters and red raspberries.

allometry.note: 1.7 m tall at 8 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
